name: ChronoScale

logo.source: chronoscale.com home page header logo (white ChronoScale wordmark on transparent PNG, 900x172); no Wikipedia page exists. Saved composited on the brand's own near-black (#0B0B0B, the background of the site's icon) with padding, 1020x292, because the official mark is white and would vanish on a light page

description: ChronoScale rents out dedicated Nvidia H100 GPU capacity for AI work from its own servers placed in rented space at three third-party data centers in Colorado, Minnesota and Utah (about 14 MW of rented capacity, 6,144 GPUs). Until August 2026 it had a single customer, Together AI, that paid a fixed per-GPU per-hour rate billed monthly; in the quarter to August 31, 2026 it also resold GPU hardware to a second customer, which made revenue jump 148 percent to $41.5M. It is a controlled company: Applied Digital, the data center developer, spun the unit out into a Nasdaq shell (the old Ekso Bionics) in May 2026, still owns about 97 percent at closing, funds it through a demand loan of up to $100M and charges it 1 percent of revenue. The bet is a pivot from a tiny single-customer GPU renter to a larger neocloud: a roughly 50 MW Microsoft GB300 contract (deliveries due February and March 2027), a 4 MW Baseten deployment and a stated target of $1bn annualized run-rate revenue by calendar Q3 2027, all conditional on financing and construction. It remains loss-making, with a $24.9M operating loss on $41.5M of revenue in the latest quarter.

hq.note: 2440 Sand Hill Road, Suite 400 (moved 2026-08-06); incorporated in Nevada

employees.note: About 31 full-time employees in the Cloud Business; the legacy Ekso unit had 53 full-time and 4 part-time, and was sold 2026-09-30 (FY2026 10-K)

businessLines.name: Dedicated GPU cloud capacity (managed cloud infrastructure services)
businessLines.how: The customer pays a fixed per-GPU, per-hour rate, billed and paid monthly, for dedicated H100 capacity under a short renewable term; ChronoScale owns the GPUs (mostly financed by finance leases) and pays the data center landlord for space and power. There is no usage upside today and revenue disappears with the one contract.
businessLines.description: Company-owned NVIDIA H100 GPU clusters hosted at three third-party colocation centers (about 14 MW rented), leased to AI developers as dedicated capacity. One customer at 2026-05-31: Together AI, across all three sites.

revenue.note: FY2025 $84.376M (-15%, from losing a customer in December 2024). Q1 FY2027 (three months to 2026-08-31) revenue $41.482M vs $16.718M (+148%). The split between GPU rental and hardware resale in Q1 FY2027 is not disclosed in the 10-Q.

businessLines.revenueNote: FY2025 $84.376M (-15%, from losing a customer in December 2024). Q1 FY2027 (three months to 2026-08-31) revenue $41.482M vs $16.718M (+148%). The split between GPU rental and hardware resale in Q1 FY2027 is not disclosed in the 10-Q.

operatingProfit.period: FY2026 operating loss (whole company: revenue $71.6M, cost of revenue $88.7M, SG&A $19.8M)
operatingProfit.note: No separate profit by line. Q1 FY2027 operating loss $(24.887)M on $41.482M revenue (Adjusted EBITDA $6.0M in the 10-Q table vs $5.9M in the press release). Cost of revenue is high because depreciation of finance-leased GPUs sits in it.

businessLines.name: One-time GPU hardware resale and support
businessLines.how: ChronoScale buys the hardware and sells it on to the customer, recognized gross at the point of transfer (it acts as principal for hardware); support and maintenance services are arranged as agent and recognized net. One-off, not recurring.
businessLines.description: Sale of GPU-related hardware to a customer plus arranging support and maintenance services, booked in the quarter to 2026-08-31.
businessLines.revenueNote: Included in the $41.482M Q1 FY2027 total; not separately disclosed. About $22.4M of hardware purchase cost is stated in the 10-Q cost-of-revenue discussion.

businessLines.name: Planned: GPU-as-a-Service, Token Factory and ChronoScale Foundry
businessLines.how: Token Factory is planned as pre-paid, per-token usage billing; GPU-as-a-Service as contracted dedicated capacity; Foundry and Outcome Engineers as platform and service fees. None yet earning revenue.
businessLines.description: GPU-as-a-Service (dedicated GPUs under contract), Token Factory (managed inference billed per token, usage-based), ChronoScale Foundry (managed enterprise agentic-AI platform) and Outcome Engineers (implementation services). Nutanix partnership announced 2026-08-18 (to be implemented through definitive agreements).
businessLines.revenueNote: Described by the 10-K as forward-looking and not yet in results

businessLines.name: Legacy Ekso Bionics (discontinued; sold 2026-09-30)
businessLines.how: Equipment sales to clinics and industrial customers plus service; no longer part of the company.
businessLines.description: Robotic exoskeletons for rehabilitation, personal mobility and industry. The EksoWorks industrial unit went to DynaWear Tech, Inc. and the neuro-rehabilitation business (Ekso Bionics, Inc.) to WanderEkso Inc., a subsidiary of Wandercraft SAS.

revenue.note: Loss from discontinued operations $1.0M FY2026 and $16.1M in Q1 FY2027

businessLines.revenueNote: Loss from discontinued operations $1.0M FY2026 and $16.1M in Q1 FY2027
